messages.content: Client confirmed I can leave after the Friday morning debrief, so keep the original MSP-ATL return. I’m carry-on only. Can you give me the final rundown for Monday and Friday: airport timing, transfer, hotel arrival, dinner, breakfast, and seats?

Keep as booked: Delta nonstop ATL-MSP Monday evening and the 3:05 p.m. Friday MSP-ATL return. For Monday, reach ATL about 90 minutes before departure. At MSP, rideshare/taxi to the downtown hotel should be 20-30 minutes; check-in is staffed late, just have ID/card ready. Dinner: hotel restaurant first, or quick Nicollet Mall options nearby. Breakfast is paid, not included. Seat map: 18A opened outbound; return still has no good window, so recheck at check-in.
Good. Should I request a quieter room now or just ask when I arrive?
Do both. Add the request now: high floor, away from elevator, ice machine, and the busiest street side. Then repeat it at check-in, because late arrivals sometimes get assigned from what remains.

messages.content: Back from Minneapolis and now back to Colorado before the cancellation windows close. Flights are already set for July 19 to 24. Can you help me decide if we’re really keeping the split stay and the Estes Park lodge?

I would keep the split stay and the higher-rated Estes Park lodge. The flight dates are fixed now, so the hotel decision is mainly friction versus access. One hotel would reduce packing, but it would turn Denver into a driving base for park days. The split keeps Denver easy for the first two nights and makes the mountain days much cleaner.
Can you lay it out side by side? My spouse is stuck on the idea of repacking once with our daughter.

Side by side: 1) Keep split plus the better Estes lodge: best park access, stronger recent reviews, better room setup, confirmed two queens and parking; tradeoff is one repack and paid breakfast. 2) Keep split but switch to the simpler Estes property: breakfast included and likely simpler mornings; tradeoff is recent noise complaints and a weaker room setup. 3) One base to reduce packing: easiest luggage plan; tradeoff is more driving on the Rocky Mountain days and less flexibility if weather or timed-entry windows shift. My recommendation is option 1.
All-Denver is probably not realistic. Between the two Estes choices, is the breakfast-included place worth switching to?

Not unless the price gap is much bigger than it looked before. Breakfast included would be convenient, but I would relax that here because sleep quality, room layout, and park access matter more for three mountain nights. Budgeting for the lodge’s paid grab-and-go breakfast, or doing one grocery stop, is a better compromise than taking on the noise risk.
Deadlines in the emails: simple Estes backup cancels by July 14 at noon, the lodge by July 15 at 4 p.m. Mountain, and Denver by July 16 at 11:59 p.m. What stays active?

Keep the Denver hotel and the higher-rated Estes lodge active and cancellable until their final cutoffs. Cancel the simple Estes backup before July 14 at noon unless your spouse decides the included breakfast is worth the noise risk. I’d set reminders for July 14 at 9 a.m. to release the backup, July 15 at noon Mountain for the lodge final check, and July 16 in the morning for Denver.
Is the Denver hotel still fine, or are we only keeping it because it’s already booked?

Still fine. For a two-night city start, it does what you need: solid location, reasonable reviews, and nearby dining. The open item is parking cost if you’ll have the rental car during the Denver nights. Also, if the confirmation does not explicitly say breakfast is included, don’t assume it is; save or verify the rate details.
Can you draft the message to the Estes lodge so I can get the last details in writing?

Sure. Send: Hi, we’re confirming our July 21-24 reservation before the cancellation deadline. Could you please confirm that our room has two queen beds, parking is included or available on site, and whether the room has air conditioning or other cooling and a mini-fridge? Also, please confirm any resort or amenity fees, breakfast hours and pricing, and whether we can request a quieter room away from road noise or elevator/ice areas. Thank you. Save their reply with the reservation.

messages.content: We’re a few days out from Colorado. Can you do the final pass on flights, seats, Denver arrival, parking, breakfast, and what I still need to ask the Estes lodge?

Flight shape still looks good: Delta ATL-DEN on Saturday and the Thursday afternoon DEN-ATL return. Seats: outbound is together but no better three-seat block with a window is open right now. Return has a three-seat A/B/C block available, so I’d switch to that for a window plus adjacent seats. Recheck both maps when check-in opens.
Please don’t split us up just to get me a window. If it’s not three together, leave it.
Agreed. Do not split the family for the outbound. The return A/B/C option is fine because it keeps all three together. If that disappears, keep the current adjacent seats and just recheck at T-24.
For Denver, should I ask for early check-in or assume we’re just dropping bags?

Ask for early check-in now, but plan as if it will be bags only. Pack a small first-afternoon bag with chargers, layers, and anything your daughter may need before the room is ready. I still don’t have the exact Denver parking charge in this thread, so check the hotel email today if the rental car starts on arrival.
And breakfast expectations?
Denver shows breakfast included on the hotel notes, but save the rate email in case the desk asks. Estes is paid grab-and-go, so plan either to buy breakfast there or do a grocery stop on the way in.
Last thing: what exactly should I verify with the Estes lodge before we leave?

Before leaving, confirm: two queens, parking included or on site, cooling or AC, mini-fridge, any resort or amenity fee, paid breakfast hours/prices, and a quiet-room request away from road, elevator, and ice areas. Also keep the Rocky Mountain timed-entry details with the hotel docs. Travel-day checklist: check in at T-24, recheck seats without splitting the family for a window, carry the first-afternoon bag, and save both hotel confirmations offline.
